summary: This article explains how a plane's curved wings, its engines, and the pilot's controls work together to lift a heavy aircraft into the sky and keep it there.
introduce: Read the title “How Airplanes Fly” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a strong forward push made by an engine
a force that slows something down as it moves through air or water
how high something is above the ground or sea level

challengeTerms.def: a movable part near a wing's tip that helps tilt a plane left or right
a strong material made by combining two or more different materials
the layer of gases that surrounds a planet

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that flying in an airplane is one of the safest ways to travel? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the four forces of flight work together to keep a plane in the air.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review thrust, drag, and altitude, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use aileron, composite, and atmosphere in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
